architectureDecisions.decision: B112 establishes a deterministic CI/test verification boundary so dependency-backed verification has a reproducible execution path outside the authoring workspace.
details: CI installs from the lockfile before verification.
Server and E2E suites have explicit bounded execution budgets.
Verification metadata is retained as a build artifact while production preview fixtures remain disabled.

architectureDecisions.decision: B110 centralizes mobile network resilience in a shared client policy without changing server authority.
details: Idempotent requests may retry within bounded attempts; ordinary mutations do not automatically retry.
Requests carry bounded correlation metadata and payload/response size guards.
Auth failures remain non-retryable and continue through the existing auth-expiry handler.

architectureDecisions.decision: M312 adds Gemini multimodal analysis behind the existing Dami ScamCheck image boundary without replacing the OpenAI default.
details: DAMI_AI_PROVIDER/NEXA_AI_PROVIDER selects the provider server-side; Gemini remains disabled unless explicitly enabled and configured.
Gemini vision uses a dedicated GEMINI_VISION_MODEL setting with GEMINI_MODEL fallback.
NEXA validates JPEG/PNG/WebP base64 input and applies a 12 MB raw-image cap before loading the Gemini SDK.
ScamCheck remains analysis-only and receives no action-execution authority from the provider.

architectureDecisions.decision: Vendor subscription hardening preserves a strict separation from NEXA Membership while centralizing vendor entitlement, payment recovery, Inbox reminders, launch-offer operations and account-closure cleanup.
details: Marketplace vendor access uses vendorEntitlement as the canonical server-side guard; legacy active vendor state is accepted only when no subscription history exists.
Failed or cancelled vendor payment attempts can be retried without creating a subscription period until provider verification succeeds.
Day-25 reminders route through the existing NEXA Inbox notification action with a stable subscription-period dedupe key.
Launch-offer allocation counts and individual allocation records are exposed only through an administrator operations endpoint.
Closing an account deactivates its vendor, expires active vendor periods and cancels pending vendor subscription payments while retaining historical records.
